artworks.title: Plate Number 147. Descending stairs and turning with a water jar on right shoulder
artworks.description: This is a series of black and white frames showing a figure in motion pouring water. The frames are arranged in rows, capturing the movement step-by-step. Each frame shows subtle changes in posture as the subject walks, tilts the container, and lifts it to pour. The background is a uniform backdrop. The image invites the viewer to observe the nuances of the figure's movement in detail.

artworks.title: Plate Number 148. Descending stairs, turning carrying a bucket of water and a broom
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequential series depicting motion. The image shows multiple frames arranged in two rows, each showing a person carrying items, presumably buckets, while ascending and descending a set of stairs. The frames capture individual moments of movement in detail. The background consists of a gridded backdrop. The black and white tones suggest an experimental era. The arrangement and scientific approach highlight the study of motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 149. Descending stairs and stooping to lift a pitcher
artworks.description: The image is a series of frames capturing a woman descending steps. She is naked and depicted in various poses as she moves downwards. The woman has dark hair tied up at the back, and her face is not clearly visible. The setting includes steps and a jug placed at different positions, with a striped background adding depth to the composition.

artworks.title: Plate Number 150. Descending stairs, stooping, lifting a pitcher and turning
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence of motion studies. A grid of 24 black and white images captures the movement of a figure stepping up and down a low platform while holding a round container. The scene features a background with horizontal stripes. Each frame shows a subtle transition as the figure transfers weight and shifts position. The repetition and framing suggest a scientific or analytical approach to capturing human movement.

artworks.title: Plate Number 151. Descending a stepladder and turning around with a rock in hands
artworks.description: This is a photograph of sequential motion studies. The image captures a series of figures in motion, aligned in two rows, taken from side and back views respectively. Each frame shows incremental progressions of a figure stepping on a small staircase while holding an object. The background consists of lined grids. The lighting is consistent throughout the sequence.

artworks.title: Plate Number 152. Jumping, running straight high jump
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a series of sequential frames capturing a high jump over a horizontal barrier. The top row shows the jump from a side profile, while the bottom row shows it from a frontal perspective. Each frame captures a different phase of the action, highlighting movement and form. The frames collectively document the detailed progression of the jump.

artworks.title: Plate Number 153. Jumping, running straight high jump
artworks.description: This is a series of sequential images showing the motion of a figure jumping over a hurdle. The image consists of two rows of six frames each, depicting a side and back view of the movement involved in the high jump. The top row shows the figure moving from a running start to lifting off the ground, arching over the hurdle, and landing on the other side. The lower row gives a perspective from behind, illustrating the same sequence of movements. The images are black and white and appear to be motion studies, capturing the fluidity and dynamics of the sporting action frozen into discrete moments.

artworks.title: Plate Number 154. Jumping, running straight high jump
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence of images capturing motion. The image consists of two rows, each showing a series of still frames depicting a subject in motion. In the top row, the subject appears to be captured in various stages of high jumping or hurdling over a bar, displaying the progression of motion from preparation to landing. The second row features the same subject in full sprint, likely at the end of the jump sequence, with frames highlighting running and leaping over a set height. The images are in black and white, giving a scientific or analytical feel. The structured and sequential layout emphasizes the detailed mechanics of the movements depicted.

artworks.title: Plate Number 156. Jumping, running straight high jump
Plate Number 157. Jumping, running twist high jump
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of sequential images capturing movement. The image consists of a grid of still frames showing sequences of motion. In the top sequence, the frames depict a progression of athletic jumps over an object, capturing every phase from the crouch, leap, and landing. Each frame in this sequence is numbered and the actions flow chronologically from left to right. In the bottom sequence, a similar set of movement is captured, showing various stages of an athletic maneuver or activity outdoors, each stage carefully documented in sequence. The photographs collectively illustrate the meticulous capturing of motion in a study of the dynamic movement. The details are relatively detailed with distinct lighting and settings for both sequences.

artworks.title: Plate Number 158. Jumping, running twist high jump
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence capturing motion through frames. The image shows black and white frames arranged in two rows, documenting the movement of an athlete jumping over a high bar and throwing an object. The sequential actions are shown with slight variations between each frame, illustrating the athlete's progression through the movements.

artworks.title: Plate Number 159. Jumping, running broad jump
artworks.description: This is a grid of sequential black and white images showing dynamic motion of a figure. The top row captures a figure in mid-air in a leaping motion with varied limb positions and body tension. The bottom row shows a similar sequence with an outdoor background featuring a path, fence, and vegetation. This work showcases the study of movement over a brief period.

artworks.title: Plate Number 160. Jumping, running broad jump
artworks.description: This is a black and white photograph featuring two rows of images capturing different stages of a jump. The top row shows a progressive jump against a lined background, while the bottom row offers a sequence from different perspectives with a natural background. Each sequence displays detailed phases of motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 161. Jumping, standing high jump
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence showing a person in motion. The image captures a series of photographic frames depicting the detailed motion of a figure engaged in a physical action, set against the backdrop of a gridded wall. Each frame in the sequence highlights different stages of the leap, documenting the bodily dynamics and postures from various angles.

artworks.title: Plate Number 163. Jumping, standing broad jump
artworks.description: This is a series of twenty-four black-and-white photographs showing the stages of jumping. The photographs appear to depict the same person in different points of a jump, transitioning from a stationary position to a leap and return. The person appears to have pale skin and short hair, and they only wear a small underwear-like garment. The photographs are in three rows: two rows of six and one row of twelve. The photos in the first two rows are larger, and show the person from the side, facing the right. The twelve photographs in the bottom row are thinner and show the person facing us and jumping again. The background features a grid pattern.

artworks.title: Plate Number 164. Jumping and pole-vaulting
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a pole vault sequential motion study. The image features a collage of black and white frames showing different stages of a pole vault, from the approach to the take-off, mid-air vault, and landing. The background is a simple indoor setting with a patterned wall. The frames are organized in a grid to depict the motion sequence.

artworks.title: Plate Number 165. Jumping and pole-vaulting
artworks.description: This photograph is a sequence of pole vaulting. It shows two rows of smaller frames capturing the detailed progression of the pole vault. The upper row shows the subject approaching the pole, jumping, completing the vault over the bar, and landing. The lower row displays a similar sequence from a slightly different angle, offering another perspective on the action. The background features a plain backdrop that directs focus to the movement of the vaulting activity, showcasing the dynamic motion and athleticism. The series demonstrates the precise and fluid movement of the pole vault, providing a step-by-step breakdown of the action.

artworks.title: Plate Number 166. Jumping over a man's back (leapfrog)
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of motion studies. It captures a sequence of images arranged in two rows, each depicting figures engaged in dynamic movements. In the top row, a figure appears to be leaping over another, showcasing a progression of a jump with varying stages of elevation and descent. The bottom row shows a progression of a piggyback ride, highlighting the lifting and carrying movement between figures. The setting is stripped down and functional, likely focusing on the study of human motion. The background is marked with vertical lines, possibly for measuring movement. The entire composition reflects an analytic, scientific approach to capturing motion in a photographic timeline.

artworks.title: Plate Number 167. Jumping over a boy's back (leapfrog)
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a sequence of a leapfrog activity. It consists of sixteen small frames arranged in a 4x4 grid, capturing moments in the progression of a leapfrog motion. The sequence is in black and white, illustrating stages of movement from approaching the bent figure, hands placed on the back, leaping over, and landing on the other side. The background features a lined surface.

artworks.title: Plate Number 168. Jumping over a boy's back (leapfrog)
artworks.description: This is a photograph of two individuals vaulting and jumping. The image shows a sequence of frames in two rows illustrating the progression of motion. Each row depicts stages of an action similar to leapfrogging in a series of stills. The black and white images are numbered and aligned with a grid and curtain backdrop. The image offers a detailed view of dynamic activity, reflecting the study of motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 169. Jumping over boy's back (leapfrog)
Plate Number 171. Stepping up on a trestle, jumping down and turning
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequential motion study involving a figure interacting with a bench-like structure. The image is organized into a grid with multiple series of photographs showing the progressive stages of a dynamic movement. The first series shows the figure taking a step onto a platform, transitioning into an athletic leap. The second series provides a rear view, capturing a similar sequence from a different perspective. The third series repeats the motion again, from yet another angle, providing a full view of the kinetic process. The backdrop appears to be an outdoor area with horizontal and vertical lines adding to the composition. The photographs are taken to study the nuances of movement, emphasizing physical form and body in action.

artworks.title: Plate Number 172. Stepping up on a trestle, jumping down and turning
artworks.description: This is a series of black and white photographs arranged in a grid format. The frames show a person in flowing fabric climbing and moving over a stool. The background has vertical lines, possibly a studio setting. The images showcase the details of human movement.

artworks.title: Plate Number 173. Ascending steps and jumping off
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequential motion study. The image consists of two panels, each displaying a series of black and white photographs capturing a figure in motion. In the top panel, the sequence shows the figure stepping onto and ascending a set of stairs, while in the bottom panel, the figures are descending down stairs and jumping. Each step and slight movement is captured in individual frames, highlighting the detailed progression of motion. The figure, dressed in a long flowing garment, is consistently positioned against a plain background to maintain focus on the movement.
